title: Attention Is All You Need
q: What BLEU score did the Transformer attain on the WMT 2014 English-to-German task in 'Attention Is All You Need'?
answer: According to 'Attention Is All You Need', the Transformer achieved a BLEU score of 28.4 on the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task. This result surpassed existing benchmark results, including ensemble architectures, by more than 2 BLEU points.

title: Combinets: Creativity via Recombination of Neural Networks
q: What novel method is introduced by Matthew Guzdial and Mark O. Riedl in their 2018 Combinets paper?
answer: Matthew Guzdial and Mark O. Riedl introduced a method called 'conceptual expansion' in their paper 'Combinets: Creativity via Recombination of Neural Networks'. This framework provides a general representation for reusing existing trained neural networks to synthesize new models without relying on backpropagation.

title: Recursive Language Models
q: How far beyond standard context limits can RLMs scale according to 'Recursive Language Models'?
answer: According to 'Recursive Language Models', the RLM paradigm enables LLMs to process inputs up to two orders of magnitude beyond their standard context windows. This substantial context expansion is achieved while maintaining a cost comparable to alternative approaches.

title: Agentic Code Reasoning
q: How does semi-formal reasoning differ from traditional chain-of-thought according to the paper 'Agentic Code Reasoning'?
answer: According to 'Agentic Code Reasoning', semi-formal reasoning differs from unstructured chain-of-thought by acting as a strict certificate. It obligates the agent to establish explicit premises and trace execution paths, preventing the model from skipping cases or asserting unsupported claims.

title: All elementary functions from a single binary operator
q: According to the paper 'All elementary functions from a single binary operator', what operations and constants can be constructed using eml(x, y) and 1?
answer: In 'All elementary functions from a single binary operator', the operator eml(x, y) = exp(x) - ln(y) paired with the constant 1 generates the standard repertoire of a scientific calculator. This includes key constants such as e, pi, and i, as well as fundamental arithmetic operations like addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, and exponentiation. It also covers conventional algebraic and transcendental functions, such as square roots, trigonometric functions, and logarithms.

title: EMO: Pretraining Mixture of Experts for Emergent Modularity
q: How does EMO encourage expert modularity during pretraining without using human-defined priors?
answer: According to 'EMO: Pretraining Mixture of Experts for Emergent Modularity', EMO achieves modularity by restricting all tokens within a single document to select experts from a shared pool, while allowing different documents to select from different pools. This mechanism leverages document boundaries alone during pretraining to foster coherent expert groupings without any human-defined priors.

title: NeoMME: A Single-Tower Multimodal-Native Multilingual Foundation Encoder for Efficient Fine-Tuning and Inference
q: What pretraining objective and context window size are used for the NeoMME foundation models?
answer: As detailed in 'NeoMME: A Single-Tower Multimodal-Native Multilingual Foundation Encoder for Efficient Fine-Tuning and Inference', both the 260M and 800M variants are pretrained from scratch using a masked discrete-diffusion text objective conditioned on visible image patches. Both models support an extensive context window of 16,384 tokens, providing enough capacity to encode up to two standard 4K UHD images.

title: SPD: Single Pass Decoding for Generative Reranking
q: How does the decoding method proposed in 'SPD: Single Pass Decoding for Generative Reranking' work mathematically and architecturally?
answer: The method in 'SPD: Single Pass Decoding for Generative Reranking' uses a lightweight self-attention head to read an N x K item-position score matrix directly from the LLM's prefill hidden states. It then decodes the ordinals as the optimal bipartite assignment of that matrix using the Hungarian algorithm, producing a valid permutation by construction in O(1) forward passes.

title: Why is AI-generated language so hard to understand?
q: In the paper 'Why is AI-generated language so hard to understand?', what did the authors find regarding all nine frontier and near-frontier models when compared to human writing?
answer: In 'Why is AI-generated language so hard to understand?', the authors evaluated nine frontier and near-frontier language models against human writing. They found that all nine models consistently used more low-frequency n-grams as well as more inanimate subjects paired with animate verbs. These patterns emerged across diverse domains, showing a widespread departure from human lexical norms.

title: Causal inference in staggered adoption panels: The correct comparison set depends on your intervention
q: Which popular causal inference methods do Lundberg and Xu note are commonly used for staggered adoption designs?
answer: In their paper 'Causal inference in staggered adoption panels: The correct comparison set depends on your intervention', Lundberg and Xu highlight difference in difference, fixed effects, matching, and synthetic control as popular methods used in staggered adoption settings. These methods compare treated adopters with non-adopters to estimate untreated counterfactual outcomes.

title: Sharp Stability of Brenier Potentials and its Link to Poincaré Inequalities
q: What optimal transport stability result is established in 'Sharp Stability of Brenier Potentials and its Link to Poincaré Inequalities'?
answer: The paper 'Sharp Stability of Brenier Potentials and its Link to Poincaré Inequalities' establishes a sharp stability bound for Brenier potentials. Given a fixed uniformly log-concave source measure, this bound governs how Brenier potentials behave under variations of the target measure.

title: Social signals dominate clinician trust in medical AI
q: What framework did Astobiza et al. introduce in their study 'Social signals dominate clinician trust in medical AI'?
answer: In 'Social signals dominate clinician trust in medical AI', Astobiza and colleagues introduced the SPOT (Synergistic Process-Outcome Trust) framework. SPOT is a Bayesian framework designed to model trust formation as an inference over latent agent properties derived from both process and outcome signals.

title: Letter to a Young Black Mathematician: History, Storytelling, and Belonging in Mathematics
q: What specific project serves as the lens for the discussion in the 2026 arXiv preprint arXiv:2611.00125?
answer: In the preprint arXiv:2611.00125, titled 'Letter to a Young Black Mathematician: History, Storytelling, and Belonging in Mathematics', the discussion is grounded in the project 'Hidden Figures Revealed'. This project documents the history and contributions of Black mathematicians at The Ohio State University.

title: Yet another approach to measuring distance in some hyperspaces
q: What completeness result is established in the paper 'Yet another approach to measuring distance in some hyperspaces'?
answer: The paper 'Yet another approach to measuring distance in some hyperspaces' proves that the defined partial metric spaces are complete if and only if the underlying metric spaces from which the ball spaces originate are complete. This establishes an exact equivalence between the completeness of the base space and that of the hyperspace.

title: Guide to Teaching with Data in Statistics and Data Science Classrooms
q: What kind of recommendations do the authors provide in 'Guide to Teaching with Data in Statistics and Data Science Classrooms'?
answer: In their paper 'Guide to Teaching with Data in Statistics and Data Science Classrooms', the authors provide empirically and theoretically supported recommendations for incorporating data into teaching. These recommendations are designed to guide educators through common pedagogical and logistical hurdles when selecting and preparing data for coursework.

title: SAWs, trails, kites, patterns
q: Under what straightforward graph conditions does the paper 'SAWs, trails, kites, patterns' state that μ equals μ_T?
answer: According to 'SAWs, trails, kites, patterns', the equality μ = μ_T holds immediately if the graph G is a tree. It also holds immediately whenever G has degree 3 or less.

title: Siegel-Weil type identities for general linear groups related to parabolic induction from two Speh representations
q: In their paper on Siegel-Weil type identities for general linear groups, what condition do Ginzburg and Soudry impose on the two Speh representations?
answer: According to Ginzburg and Soudry's paper 'Siegel-Weil type identities for general linear groups related to parabolic induction from two Speh representations', the two Speh representations are attached to parabolic induction such that both correspond to the same irreducible, cuspidal representation.

title: Calibrated Multiaccuracy: Deterministic and Randomized Sample Complexity
q: What is the sample complexity of randomized calibrated multiaccuracy established by Lu, Noarov, and Roth (2026)?
answer: In 'Calibrated Multiaccuracy: Deterministic and Randomized Sample Complexity', Lu, Noarov, and Roth show that the sample complexity for ε-calibrated multiaccuracy using a randomized predictor is ~Θ(log|G|/ε^2 + 1/ε^(5/2)). This upper bound is achieved via an algorithm producing randomized predictors. Consequently, it strictly separates the sample complexity of calibrated multiaccuracy from the ~Θ(log|G|/ε^2 + 1/ε^3) complexity required for full multicalibration.

title: Technofascism: AI, Big Tech, and the new authoritarianism
q: What is the primary argument presented in the paper 'Technofascism: AI, Big Tech, and the new authoritarianism'?
answer: The primary argument of 'Technofascism: AI, Big Tech, and the new authoritarianism' is that features of contemporary digital technologies, their governance, and their broader political context mirror historical fascist phenomena. Although promoted as innovative milestones, these transformations introduce control mechanisms and ideological patterns reminiscent of fascism.

title: Partisan responsiveness in real time: causal evidence from Trump’s military attack on Iran
q: What core research question does the paper 'Partisan responsiveness in real time: causal evidence from Trump’s military attack on Iran' address?
answer: In 'Partisan responsiveness in real time: causal evidence from Trump’s military attack on Iran', the authors examine whether the effects of elite cues on public opinion occur in real time. Specifically, they test how rapidly citizens adopt partisan interpretations following an unexpected political event.

title: Irrational exuberance and neural crash warning signals during endogenous experimental market bubbles
q: According to the paper 'Irrational exuberance and neural crash warning signals during endogenous experimental market bubbles', what role did the nucleus accumbens (NAcc) play during price bubbles?
answer: In 'Irrational exuberance and neural crash warning signals during endogenous experimental market bubbles', the authors found that activity in the nucleus accumbens (NAcc) tracked the price bubble and predicted future price changes. Furthermore, traders who bought more aggressively in response to NAcc signals ended up earning less.

title: Foraging synchrony drives resilience in human–dolphin mutualism
q: According to 'Foraging synchrony drives resilience in human–dolphin mutualism', how do fishers benefit from synchronizing with dolphins?
answer: According to 'Foraging synchrony drives resilience in human–dolphin mutualism', dolphins herd migratory mullet schools toward the coast, bringing prey within reach of net-casting fishers. The fishers gain higher foraging success specifically when they synchronize their net-casting behavior with the foraging cues given by the dolphins.

title: Fine and ultrafine Martian dust presents additional risks for future crewed missions to Mars
q: What specific methodology did Scott J. VanBommel and colleagues use to inspect Martian dust in their 2026 PNAS report?
answer: In their 2026 PNAS paper, 'Fine and ultrafine Martian dust presents additional risks for future crewed missions to Mars,' VanBommel and colleagues conducted a direct examination using X-ray fluorescence. They analyzed and modeled observational data gathered directly by NASA's Perseverance rover on Mars. This approach allowed them to evaluate particulates that had settled onto calibration targets and spacesuit material samples.

title: The value of diversity and the diversity of values in science
q: In 'The value of diversity and the diversity of values in science', what specific prior proposal published in BioScience do the authors challenge?
answer: In 'The value of diversity and the diversity of values in science', the authors challenge a recent proposal in BioScience advocating that scientists restore a value-free ideal. That proposal was framed as a defense against attacks labeling research as 'left-wing science', which Witteveen and Elliott argue is the wrong strategy.

title: Is parents’ employment uncertainty linked to children's development? Analysing patterns and mechanisms in France
q: What dataset and empirical methods were used by Facchini, Panico, and Barone to evaluate parental employment uncertainty in France?
answer: In 'Is parents’ employment uncertainty linked to children's development? Analysing patterns and mechanisms in France,' the authors analyze four waves of the nationally representative French Longitudinal Study of Children (ELFE). Their empirical approach combines ordinary least squares and linear probability models with counterfactual mediation analysis, alongside regression-with-residuals to account for post-treatment confounders such as sibling birth.

title: Varying the Content of Political Science Surveys to Improve the Survey Experience and Data Quality of Politically Disengaged Respondents
q: Where and when was the paper 'Varying the Content of Political Science Surveys to Improve the Survey Experience and Data Quality of Politically Disengaged Respondents' published?
answer: The study 'Varying the Content of Political Science Surveys to Improve the Survey Experience and Data Quality of Politically Disengaged Respondents' was published on August 11, 2026. It appeared in the Journal of Survey Statistics and Methodology under DOI 10.1093/jssam/smaf061.

title: Multi-periodic photonic mechanism for non-spectral magenta coloration in Anna's hummingbird ( Calypte anna ) feathers
q: According to Kim et al. (2026), what structural material embeds the melanosomes in Anna's hummingbird feathers?
answer: According to the paper by Kim et al. (2026), the platelet-shaped melanosomes are embedded in corneous beta-protein. This multi-layered composite architecture facilitates the light interference responsible for iridescent feather coloration.

title: timePlex: Increasing mass spectrometry throughput using time-encoded sample multiplexing
q: In 'timePlex: Increasing mass spectrometry throughput using time-encoded sample multiplexing', how does time-domain multiplexing interact with mass-domain multiplexing?
answer: In 'timePlex: Increasing mass spectrometry throughput using time-encoded sample multiplexing', the authors explain that time-domain multiplexing is completely orthogonal to isotopic mass-domain multiplexing such as plexDIA. Because of this orthogonality, the two approaches can be combined combinatorially across the mass and time domains. This synergy scales throughput multiplicatively rather than linearly.

title: Emigration and radical right populism
q: According to the paper 'Emigration and radical right populism', what are the two main mechanisms connecting emigration to PRR success?
answer: In 'Emigration and radical right populism', the authors argue that emigration affects elections through two complementary mechanisms. First, the departure of citizens alters the composition of local electorates, and second, it changes the political and policy preferences of the citizens who are left behind.

title: Stress‐Testing the “Universities Without Walls” Vision 2030: Lessons From Displaced Ukrainian Universities in Wartime
q: What specific sample of institutions was examined in the 2024–2025 audit presented in 'Stress‐Testing the “Universities Without Walls” Vision 2030: Lessons From Displaced Ukrainian Universities in Wartime'?
answer: The study 'Stress‐Testing the “Universities Without Walls” Vision 2030: Lessons From Displaced Ukrainian Universities in Wartime' analyzed a comprehensive audit conducted in 2024–2025. The sample comprised all 21 relocated Ukrainian universities that were operating predominantly online at the time of the investigation.

title: Sponge Carrying by Dolphins (Delphinidae, Tursiops sp.): A Foraging Specialization Involving Tool Use?
q: Which sponge species was documented being carried by bottlenose dolphins in the paper by Smolker et al. (1997)?
answer: According to Smolker et al. in 'Sponge Carrying by Dolphins (Delphinidae, Tursiops sp.): A Foraging Specialization Involving Tool Use?', the dolphins were observed carrying the sponge Echinodictyum mesenterinum. The animals positioned these marine sponges directly over their rostra during diving and surfacing sequences. This specific sponge species was central to the behavioral specialization analyzed throughout the study.

title: Capturing Demographic Burden Over Time with the Cumulative Dependency Ratio
q: How does the cumulative dependency ratio introduced by Marois, Lutz, and Prettner (2026) calculate demographic burden?
answer: In 'Capturing Demographic Burden Over Time with the Cumulative Dependency Ratio,' Marois, Lutz, and Prettner introduce an indicator based on a longitudinal reinterpretation of the traditional metric. It explicitly incorporates a temporal dimension by aggregating person-years lived in dependent ages relative to support ages over a specified time horizon. This approach yields a person-year-based summary of demographic burden.

title: Genomic insights into evolution of parthenogenesis and triploidy in the flowerpot snake
q: What did the newly assembled genome in 'Genomic insights into evolution of parthenogenesis and triploidy in the flowerpot snake' reveal about chromosome count and subgenomes?
answer: In 'Genomic insights into evolution of parthenogenesis and triploidy in the flowerpot snake', the authors assembled the genome of Indotyphlops braminus and revealed a total of 40 chromosomes. These chromosomes are grouped into three distinct subgenomes, designated A, B, and C. This architecture reflects the triploid genomic organization of this all-female species.

title: Antibiotic-loaded cement spacers: a comprehensive review
q: According to Riaz et al.'s paper 'Antibiotic-loaded cement spacers: a comprehensive review', what time period of literature was examined?
answer: In 'Antibiotic-loaded cement spacers: a comprehensive review', Riaz and colleagues evaluated peer-reviewed literature published between 1988 and 2024. In addition to this literature review, the authors incorporated insights from their own clinical experience.

title: Immune cell–specific SMN expression and sustained immune alterations in treated spinal muscular atrophy
q: According to the paper 'Immune cell–specific SMN expression and sustained immune alterations in treated spinal muscular atrophy', which immune cells in neonatal mouse spleens had the highest SMN levels?
answer: According to 'Immune cell–specific SMN expression and sustained immune alterations in treated spinal muscular atrophy', SMN expression in neonatal mouse spleens was highest in B cells. The authors noted that this expression was massively reduced in SMA model mice.

title: Beyond motor rescue: defining adequate SMN restoration in spinal muscular atrophy
q: In 'Beyond motor rescue: defining adequate SMN restoration in spinal muscular atrophy', what central therapeutic question does Yeo highlight?
answer: In 'Beyond motor rescue: defining adequate SMN restoration in spinal muscular atrophy', Crystal Jing Jing Yeo highlights the critical therapeutic question: 'What constitutes adequate SMN restoration?' This question emerges as disease-modifying therapies uncover an increasingly complex spectrum of residual disease biology beyond motor neuron rescue.

title: Ambivalent, biological, and cultural racism and the legitimation of inequality: Original cross-national survey evidence from the United States and The Netherlands
q: What did Wang and Mijs discover regarding the overall prevalence of racism in the United States and the Netherlands?
answer: According to the paper 'Ambivalent, biological, and cultural racism and the legitimation of inequality' by Wang and Mijs, a majority of respondents in both the United States and the Netherlands express either blatant racism or ambivalent racism. The authors define ambivalent racism as harboring conflicting attitudes toward a racial or ethnic group. This indicates that racially biased attitudes remain prevalent in both societies.

title: Life events and life satisfaction: Estimating effects of multiple life events in combined models
q: What dataset and sample size were analyzed by Krämer, Rohrer, Lucas, and Richter in their 2024 study on life satisfaction and life events?
answer: In their 2024 study 'Life events and life satisfaction: Estimating effects of multiple life events in combined models', Krämer and colleagues analyzed representative German data from the Socio-Economic Panel (SOEP). The dataset contained observations from N = 40,121 individuals covering n = 41,402 distinct event occurrences.

title: Voting for a Killer: Efraín Ríos Montt's Return to Politics in Democratic Guatemala
q: What research methodology is employed in the study 'Voting for a Killer: Efraín Ríos Montt's Return to Politics in Democratic Guatemala'?
answer: In 'Voting for a Killer: Efraín Ríos Montt's Return to Politics in Democratic Guatemala', Regina Bateson uses process tracing as her research methodology. She applies this approach to trace and explain Ríos Montt's political trajectory and comeback.

title: Authoritarian Repression and Electoral Opposition: Mobilization under Germany's Antisocialist Law
q: Which historical setting and time period are examined in Henry Thomson's 'Authoritarian Repression and Electoral Opposition'?
answer: The historical setting examined in Henry Thomson's 'Authoritarian Repression and Electoral Opposition: Mobilization under Germany's Antisocialist Law' is Imperial Germany between 1878 and 1890. During this period, the state instituted the Antisocialist Law, banning the social democratic party. Under these provisions, authoritarian authorities routinely expelled party leaders from their home electoral districts.

title: Electoral Violence, Partisan Identity, and Perceptions of Election Quality: A Survey Experiment in West Bengal, India
q: What methodological approach did Ursula Daxecker and Hanne Fjelde employ in their West Bengal election study?
answer: In 'Electoral Violence, Partisan Identity, and Perceptions of Election Quality: A Survey Experiment in West Bengal, India,' Ursula Daxecker and Hanne Fjelde conducted a vignette experiment in West Bengal following India's 2019 elections. The experiment presented survey respondents with information regarding violence while varying the partisan identity of the perpetrator.

title: Paying to Play: How Parliamentary Candidates Fund Ruling Party Campaigns in Malawi
q: How does the explanation in Wahman and Seeberg's study on Malawi campaign finance differ from conventional scholarship?
answer: Conventional scholarship typically attributes the financial dominance of ruling parties to direct abuse of state resources. In contrast, Wahman and Seeberg's 'Paying to Play' demonstrates an alternative mechanism where government parties attract affluent candidates who invest their own personal funds into parliamentary campaigns in anticipation of accessing central state resources later.

title: Varieties of Electoral Dominance
q: What problem does the paper 'Varieties of Electoral Dominance' identify regarding the concept of a 'dominant party'?
answer: The article 'Varieties of Electoral Dominance' points out that the conventional label 'dominant party' encompasses an extremely diverse set of entities. It covers cases ranging from parties capturing unremarkable vote shares in established democracies to those securing massive popular majorities in free but unfair electoral contexts.

title: Local Electoral Institutions and the Dynamic Motivations of Ethnic Party Candidate Nominations in South Africa
q: What electoral system setting is examined in the paper 'Local Electoral Institutions and the Dynamic Motivations of Ethnic Party Candidate Nominations in South Africa'?
answer: The paper 'Local Electoral Institutions and the Dynamic Motivations of Ethnic Party Candidate Nominations in South Africa' studies South Africa's local Mixed-Member Proportional electoral system. Under this institutional arrangement, parties nominate both Single Member District candidates and Proportional Representation list candidates.

title: The Socio-Structural Basis of the Long-Term Decline in Traditional Left-Right Class Voting in Affluent Democracies, 1964‐2019
q: Which hypotheses were proposed by Fernández, Jaime-Castillo, and Caihuelas Navajas regarding the decline of class-based voting in affluent democracies?
answer: In their paper 'The Socio-Structural Basis of the Long-Term Decline in Traditional Left-Right Class Voting in Affluent Democracies, 1964‐2019', Fernández, Jaime-Castillo, and Caihuelas Navajas hypothesize that the decline in voting cleavages between the working class and other classes stems from three factors. Specifically, they suggest it is linked to the shrinkage of the working class, increases in economic prosperity, and a reduction in levels of inequality.
